bullets.text: The passenger ferry MV Sable Crest sank in the Marnesh Straits on February 14, 2026, shortly after departing Halvary for Ostrem Bay.
The operative number aboard was revised from a manifest total of 218 to 241 after the operator identified unticketed foot passengers.
Investigators identified vehicle deck water ingress through an insecure bow door as the preliminary cause, and the operator suspended all straits sailings.
The ferry is observed listing in the Marnesh Straits; a distress call is received and search and rescue assets are tasked.
Ninety-six people are recovered from the water and brought ashore at Halvary.
Ninety-six people were recovered from the water in the first phase of the response.
The hospital activated its major incident plan and ambulances staged at the ferry terminal.
The MV Sable Crest capsized and sank in the Marnesh Straits.
Survivors were recovered from the water and brought ashore at Halvary by coastguard vessels, helicopters and fishing boats.
The Marnesh Coastguard tasked search and rescue assets in response to the distress call.
Multiple vessels and rescue helicopters from two stations operated on scene.
Halvary General Hospital activated its major incident plan with ambulances staging at the terminal.
